items.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: And I was at the west coast jazz party with him two years ago and just to have him just growling at me over that ride cymbal

ctx.x: I think it’s a spirit. It’s a real spirit thing. And I just want to be a part of that. And I think the only way you can be a part of that is if you’re there. You hang with that, you live with

them, you live with that music. To play with it is a totally different vibe than to sit in the audience and to listen to it. Just playing with these guys is such an eye-opener for me. These guys that I’ve been listening to on recordings, but to actually get to be a part of that creative process with them, you really end up taking a lot with you. I think Kenny Barron embodies a lot of that. I think he’s got that — he has his own voice in the music. But at the same time there’s all this tradition within him and he…
You were born with a groove. I have to say that.
